champion: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) of the skin
ordered_diagnoses: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) of the skin

facts.raw_span: A woman in her 70s with recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
presented with a pruritic rash ongoing for 2 weeks
The rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
then gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
She denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Erythematous annular plaques without scale on her right arm and bilateral legs
4-mm punch biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain was negative for fungal organisms
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating numerous scattered eosinophils

concepts.preferred_label: Immune-related adverse event (irAE) of the skin
concepts.why: The patient's recent initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen and the development of a pruritic rash suggest an immune-related adverse event of the skin.
The patient's use of pembrolizumab and the development of a rash are consistent with this diagnosis.
The patient's use of ipilimumab and the development of a rash are consistent with this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
concepts.why: The presence of eosinophils in the biopsy findings and the patient's symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis, although the lack of systemic symptoms makes it less likely.

The presence of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils, as well as the negative PAS stain for fungal organisms, points towards eosinophilic cellulitis.

rationales.F02: The patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, which are immunotherapies that can cause skin-related immune-related adverse events.
rationales.F08: The presence of erythematous annular plaques without scale on the patient's right arm and bilateral legs is consistent with a skin rash.
rationales.F09: The biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils are consistent with eosinophilic dermatitis.
rationales.F12: The presence of numerous scattered eosinophils on hematoxylin and eosin stain is consistent with eosinophilic dermatitis.
